title: Reuse all words of keyed blocks for bounded draws
question: Can fixed-block word reuse improve current-path randomization without seed replay requirements?
summary: Buffer repeated bounded draws and retain the original single-use categorical path; remove public seed inputs independently. Final native resident Fisher–Yates improves modestly; hosted effects are small and variable.

workloads: 120003-row resident Fisher–Yates, 150003-row exact allocation, 250003-row external uniform/direct controls; one worker and 32/256 MiB.
Separate 1000000-row native direct control; five native/three browser primary pairs and seven confirmation pairs.

validation.summary: Independent exact fields, ID conservation, quotas, lineage, metadata, encoded caps and cleanup; bounded-word/rejection oracle and permutation multiplicity; seed-input rejection and saved-job omission. Final native/browser checks recorded in the comparison receipt.

limitations: Small warm WSL2/ext4 and persistent bundled Chromium cells; no native Windows/macOS, installed-browser, 25-million-row or scale claim.
Initial direct control regressed; a separately scoped larger repeat did not reproduce it. Neither result establishes a direct-split gain.
External uniform shuffle has no demonstrated improvement; browser exact-allocation effect is negligible.
Raw receipts and frozen source forests are local ignored scratch artifacts; no external archive upload or public evidence publication.
Final seed-free hosted rechecks did not reproduce the initial browser gain. Probabilistic controls have overlapping ranges and small mixed effects; no probabilistic speedup is claimed.
exclusions: Failed native temporary-directory warmup and rounded timed-wait measurements.
Browser warmups with warning/path-translation verifier assumptions.
reopen_when: A current target-workload profile attributes material cost to remaining random-key generation or storage passes; require new matched complete-job evidence.
